# `pygeovision channel`

Run any of the **41 pipelines** by name: find the imagery, prepare it, compute the answer, and write rasters, vectors,
a map, tables and a report. This is the main entry point for end users; every pipeline has its own page in the
[pipeline catalogue](../../pipelines/catalog/index.md).

## When to use it

Use it when you have a question about a place and a time ("which areas flooded?", "how much forest was lost?"), not a
file. Start with `pygeovision channel list` to see every pipeline and whether it needs your trained weights.

## What you get

A folder (`-o`, default `./output/`) with the output rasters, vector files, `map.png`, report files and
`run_summary.json`. [Reading results](../../pipelines/results.md) explains each file. Rebuild reports later without
re-running with [`report`](report.md).

## Things to know

* The seven pipelines marked "needs your weights" refuse to run without `--checkpoint`; they never invent a result.
* An unknown or removed name exits with code 2 and explains why ([removed pipelines](../../pipelines/removed.md)).
* Pipelines that download imagery need a network and, for some providers, [credentials](../../data/authentication.md).
* Extra arguments are passed as `--param KEY=VALUE`.

## Worked examples

```bash
pygeovision channel list
pygeovision channel water_bodies --bbox -0.15 51.47 -0.10 51.52 --date 2024-06 -o ./output/
```

## Commands

### `pygeovision channel`

Run an end-to-end geospatial pipeline by name.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `PIPELINE_NAME` | text | yes |

**Options**

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--bbox` | number |  |  |  |
| `--output`, `-o` | text | `./pipeline_output` |  |  |
| `--date` | text |  |  | YYYY-MM acquisition date (single-date pipelines). |
| `--date-before` | text |  |  | Earlier date (bi-temporal pipelines). |
| `--date-after` | text |  |  | Later date (bi-temporal pipelines). |
| `--dates` | text |  |  | Comma-separated dates (vegetation_indices). |
| `--model` | text |  |  | Model name (pipelines that run a network). |
| `--checkpoint` | path |  |  | Your trained .pth weights; required by every 'needs_weights' pipeline. |
| `--source` | text |  |  | Data source override (land_cover: worldcover \| dynamic_world). |
| `--provider` | text |  |  | Restrict search to this provider (repeatable, e.g. --provider planetary_computer). An unrecognised name is rejected by the search layer itself, not validated here. |
| `--param` | text |  |  | Any other pipeline argument, e.g. --param anomaly_threshold=0.2 --param dem_type=cop30 (repeatable). Values are read as JSON when possible, and 5,10,15 is a list of numbers. |
| `--no-report` | flag | off |  | Skip the map, vector layers and reports (also: PYGEOVISION_REPORT=0). |
| `--report-formats` | text | `pdf,xlsx,docx` |  | Report formats: any of pdf, xlsx (Excel), docx (Word); 'none' for no reports. |
| `--vector-formats` | text | `gpkg,geojson` |  | Vector formats: any of gpkg, geojson, shp, kml; 'none' for no vector files. |
| `--class-names` | text |  |  | Comma-separated names for the classes 0,1,2... of a network you trained (labels the map, tables and vector attributes). |
| `--report-title` | text |  |  | Replace the report title. |

:::{dropdown} Full help text

```text
Usage: pygeovision channel [OPTIONS] PIPELINE_NAME

  Run an end-to-end geospatial pipeline by name.

  Downloads imagery with PyGeoFetch, then computes an index, a terrain product, a reference map,
  or runs your own trained network. ``pygeovision channel list`` shows every pipeline and
  whether it runs out of the box ("ready") or needs your trained weights ("needs_weights", pass
  --checkpoint). Removed pipelines explain why.

  Examples:
      pygeovision channel list

      pygeovision channel water_bodies \
          --bbox -0.15 51.47 -0.10 51.52 --date 2024-06

      pygeovision channel wildfire_severity \
          --bbox -122.6 39.7 -121.9 40.2 \
          --date-before 2018-10 --date-after 2018-12

      pygeovision channel building_footprints \
          --bbox -0.15 51.47 -0.10 51.52 --date 2024-06 \
          --checkpoint runs/buildings/best.pth

      pygeovision channel crop_health --bbox ... \
          --date-before 2024-05 --date-after 2024-08 --param anomaly_threshold=0.2

Options:
  --bbox MIN_LON MIN_LAT MAX_LON MAX_LAT
  -o, --output TEXT               [default: ./pipeline_output]
  --date TEXT                     YYYY-MM acquisition date (single-date pipelines).
  --date-before TEXT              Earlier date (bi-temporal pipelines).
  --date-after TEXT               Later date (bi-temporal pipelines).
  --dates TEXT                    Comma-separated dates (vegetation_indices).
  --model TEXT                    Model name (pipelines that run a network).
  --checkpoint PATH               Your trained .pth weights; required by every 'needs_weights'
                                  pipeline.
  --source TEXT                   Data source override (land_cover: worldcover | dynamic_world).
  --provider TEXT                 Restrict search to this provider (repeatable, e.g. --provider
                                  planetary_computer). An unrecognised name is rejected by the
                                  search layer itself, not validated here.
  --param KEY=VALUE               Any other pipeline argument, e.g. --param
                                  anomaly_threshold=0.2 --param dem_type=cop30 (repeatable).
                                  Values are read as JSON when possible, and 5,10,15 is a list
                                  of numbers.
  --no-report                     Skip the map, vector layers and reports (also:
                                  PYGEOVISION_REPORT=0).
  --report-formats TEXT           Report formats: any of pdf, xlsx (Excel), docx (Word); 'none'
                                  for no reports.  [default: pdf,xlsx,docx]
  --vector-formats TEXT           Vector formats: any of gpkg, geojson, shp, kml; 'none' for no
                                  vector files.  [default: gpkg,geojson]
  --class-names TEXT              Comma-separated names for the classes 0,1,2... of a network
                                  you trained (labels the map, tables and vector attributes).
  --report-title TEXT             Replace the report title.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
```
:::
